# Model overview

**MOOOD** is an open-source discrete-event simulation developed by Richard Pilbery and colleagues. It follows callers after an NHS 111 primary-care disposition and represents subsequent contact with primary care, NHS 111, ambulance services and emergency departments. The Python and SimPy model compares the existing system with timely primary-care contact and reports activity across services and avoidable ED attendance.

The original data and parameters relate to callers registered with Bradford and Airedale GP practices, so reuse elsewhere requires local review and validation.

## Actions for participants before the session

- Attempt to reproduce the model by using GitHub Codespaces (recommended for participants new to GitHub) or by cloning the [MOOOD repository](https://github.com/RichardPilbery/MOOOD-study) and running it locally; see the [repository README](https://github.com/RichardPilbery/MOOOD-study#readme) for the current build and run instructions.
- Try the model's interactive application by following the [generated documentation](https://richardpilbery.github.io/MOOOD-study/).
- Explore the repository and its structure.

::: {.callout-warning title="Local software requirement"}
**This model uses Python.** To run it locally, you will need Python installed and will need to set up the packages and environment described in the repository.
:::

## Getting help

If you have a problem running or reusing MOOOD, the model's issue tracker will be the best way to contact the ReModel team. **Issue tracker link: [to be added].** When reporting a problem, describe what you were trying to do, what happened and any error messages you received.

## Session objectives and outline

This will be a discussion session around the model and our attempts to run the model as it currently exists. Participants will discuss:

- any issues they had in running the model in its current form;
- any areas of the model they didn't understand;
- how we think the model is structured from inputs through to outputs;
- how callers, services, contacts and events are represented;
- assumptions for demand, care pathways, timely primary-care contact and subsequent service use;
- where they think this model might be useful.

The aim is for participants to leave this session with a clear understanding of how to run the model and a working version of the model that they can continue to explore before the Reuse session.
